string-array.name: rules
string-array.item: One long list of everything you have to do. New items always go at the end.
Write down whatever comes to mind without judging it. The system does the judging.
Work page by page. First read the page quickly without doing anything.
Then go through it slowly, in order, until one task “stands out” — you feel it’s ready to be done. Don’t prioritise in your head.
Work on it for as long as you like. You don’t have to finish: little and often.
Finished — “Done” or swipe right. Not finished — “Not finished” or swipe left: the task goes to the end of the list. “×2” next to a task means it has already been moved to the end twice.
Keep circling the same page until a whole pass gives you nothing. Then move on.
If you come to a page and nothing stands out on the first pass, its remaining tasks are dismissed (except on the last page, where you’re still writing). Don’t bring them back straight away.
After the last page, go back to the first page that still has tasks.
Common sense first: if something has to be done right now, do it right now — find it with search or the arrows.
Don’t use the list for things with a fixed time of day — keep those in a calendar.
Keep a separate list for each place (Home, Work). The date marks the first task added each day — it shows how things move.
After a long break, read through all outstanding tasks first.
